name: EC-SERS (Electrochemical Surface-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy) Spectral Database of Drug and Adulterant Compounds
description: EC-SERS (electrochemical surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy) spectral library of 32 drugs of abuse and adulterant compounds from the NIST Public Data Resource (Ott, NIST, 2024; doi:10.18434/mds2-3502, v1.0.1). 131 spectra, 785 nm excitation on a DropSens SPELEC silver electrode; each deposited CSV is the highest-intensity / best-resolution spectrum of one replicate acquisition. The deposit's raw potential-resolved .exp files (118) and combined Excel sheet are not loaded here. Values are 'Counts minus Dark (a.u.)' -- NOT normalized: every file has slightly negative points (dark-subtraction residuals, per-file minima -574..-16) and per-file maxima span 5.1e4-2.0e5, so expect the substrate/potential-dependent intensity drift typical of EC-SERS (realistic but not 'plain Raman'). Two acquisition batches are mixed: 96 files on a 1,014-point grid (32.6-2,859.1 cm^-1) and 35 on a 1,011-point grid (33.8-2,995.5 cm^-1), both non-uniformly spaced (1.95-4.18 cm^-1 steps); the loader interpolates all spectra onto the common 1,013-point grid (36.6-2,859.1 cm^-1) that every file fully covers. 126 of the 131 spectra carry one of 11 concentration labels (1, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100, 300, 333, 1,000, 1,001, 1,013 ppm) -- a built-in concentration / detection-limit subtask; the 5 unlabelled ones are solid-form procaine (3 replicates) and pure-powder acryl- and furanyl-fentanyl. Substances: alprazolam, cocaine, codeine, dextromethorphan, diphenhydramine, etizolam, etonitazene, fentanyl, heroin, levamisole, lidocaine, methadone, methamphetamine, morphine, nicotine, procaine (solid), quinine, sufentanil, temazepam, xylazine, 4-ANPP, buprenorphine, diltiazem, hydroxyzine, naltrexone, and six fentanyl analogs (acetyl, acryl, furanyl, methoxyacetyl, valeryl); the deposit's 33-compound analyte panel also lists mitragynine, for which no CSV is deposited. Mostly the nontargeted campaign (Ott et al. 2024, doi:10.1016/j.forc.2024.100621); the fentanyl-analog spectra (spectrum numbers 292-326) come from the targeted method (Ott et al. 2022, doi:10.3389/frans.2022.834820). group_ids = (substance, concentration, replicate): 118 groups of 1-3 spectra (106 single-spectrum), and all 24 measurements without a replicate marker at one substance+concentration share a single group (possibly the same acquisition session). 10 substances have fewer than 3 groups, so grouped k-fold CV only covers a subset of the library. Filenames are '<Substance>[_<conc>ppm][_form_solid][_nontarget][_rep<N>]_Spectrum_<n>.csv'; the deposit contains one 'Spectrum 293' with a space, one 'nontargeT' typo and one file without a target marker, all parsed by _nist_ecsers_parse_name.

rai:dataCollection: EC-SERS (electrochemical surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy) with 785 nm excitation on a DropSens SPELEC silver electrode (Metrohm potentiostat setup), NIST. The deposit contains the highest-intensity / best-resolution spectrum of each replicate as CSV; the full potential-resolved .exp files (118) are in the deposit but not loaded by raman_data.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Authors' pipeline: modified-polynomial baseline correction in DropView, then the single best spectrum per replicate exported as CSV (Origin Pro); values are 'Counts minus Dark (a.u.)', not normalized (per-file minima slightly negative, maxima 5e4-2e5). The loader additionally interpolates both native grids onto the common 1,013-point grid (36.6-2,859.1 cm^-1).
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Substance labels parsed from the deposited filenames (32 analytes); 126/131 spectra additionally carry a concentration label (1-1,013 ppm, 11 levels). No human annotation beyond the authors' sample preparation.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No personal or sensitive information is included; all spectra originate from lab-prepared chemical standards.
rai:dataBiases: EC-SERS intensities depend on the silver electrode surface and electrochemical potential, so spectra of the same substance vary in absolute intensity across replicates and batches. Two acquisition batches (1,014-pt and 1,011-pt native grids) are mixed and interpolated onto one common grid. Per-substance spectrum counts range from 1 to 13 (10 of 32 substances have fewer than 3 replicate groups), so the class balance is strongly uneven. Lab-prepared solutions, not seized street material.
rai:dataLimitations: Forensic library-formation data, not a balanced clinical or field dataset: 32 substances with 1-13 spectra each (118 replicate groups; 10 substances < 3 groups), so grouped k-fold CV covers only a subset. Concentration labels exist for 126/131 spectra (the 5 unlabelled: solid procaine x3, pure acryl-/furanyl-fentanyl). Electrochemical SERS signal is substrate/potential-dependent; models may not transfer to plain (non-enhanced) Raman or other SERS substrates.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Supports forensic drug screening research and ML benchmarking for fentanyl-analog and adulterant identification; misuse potential is limited since the data identify controlled substances rather than individuals.
rai:dataUseCases: Multi-class substance identification (32 classes), concentration / limit-of-detection regression from the 11-level concentration series, and EC-SERS spectral library formation.
